Items.Authors: Lorenzo Zago, Laurent Jolissaint
Items.Title: Advanced active optics actuator for primary mirrors exposed to dynamic wind loads
Items.Abstract: The paper presents a novel axial actuator for active optics systems in primary mirrors of telescopes operating in open-air environments and exposed to wind buffeting.   The current prototype is designed as a force-feedback actuator with a maximum force of 500 N and a resolution better than 0.1 N, consistent with the performance of existing active optics axial actuators.   Its key innovation lies in its fast dynamic response, achieving a closed-loop bandwidth of 10 Hz, enabling effective compensation of wind-induced disturbances on lightweight primary mirrors installed in open-air conditions.

Items.Authors: Pablo Gutierrez Cheetham, Pablo Alberto Fuerte Rodriguez, Antonio Ramon Manescau Hernandez, Frédéric Derie
Items.Title: Advanced calibration unit electronics for VLT FORS-upgrade
Items.Abstract: FORS1 was one of the first instruments installed at the VLT, yet still in high demand. An upgrade is underway, carried out by ESO and the Astronomical Observatory of Trieste (INAF), to bring it back soon with new, advanced features.  One key feature is the ability to perform instrument calibrations at any time (day or night) without constraining telescope activities. This is achieved by projecting the calibration light internally rather than toward the back of the M3 of the VLT.  This new design features advanced electronics to control and monitor the calibration lamps (Pencil, Arc, and Halogen), incorporating specialized Beckhoff power-monitoring terminals, for voltage and current, as well as small embedded I²C bus sensors for light intensity, operating time, and temperature that can be deployed near the lamps. Also introducing a compact shutter to block the light while keeping the lamps turned on, and a Kniel EtherCAT controlled power supply.  The presentation focuses on the electronics

Items.Authors: Mahshid Shiri, Christian Eredia, Vincenzo Cianniello, Enrico Cascone
Items.Title: Advanced motion control of Stewart platforms: integrating Kane's method with nonlinear model predictive control
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a high precision motion control framework for a 6-DOF Stewart platform integrating Kane's inverse dynamics with Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) via CasADi/IPOPT. Kane feedforward provides exact actuator forces in O(216) operations. NMPC enforces force constraints over a 10 step horizon using RK4 prediction. Under 5% mass uncertainty, 3D tracking RMS is below 0.001 mm with zero solver failures across 4,500 steps. HIL validation on a BLDC motor via TwinCAT ADS confirms cascade architecture performance.

Items.Authors: Benjamin Cromey, Laura Coyle, Tyler McCracken, Jeremy Shugrue, Joseph Ho, Thomas Peters, Sebastian Valencia, Dominic Maes, Dustin Putnam, Daniel Porpora
Items.Title: Advancing critical technologies and integrated modeling for HWO in year 8 of the ULTRA program
Items.Abstract: The Ultrastable Large Telescopes Research and Analysis (ULTRA) program led by BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems continues to press forward with technology advances and system level insights for NASA’s Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). The team continues its dual focus on 1) high-fidelity simulation leveraging models provided by NASA to evaluate their capabilities and risks as potential architectures and 2) hardware demonstrations/studies to address high priority technology gaps in stable mirrors, precision thermal control, and ultrastable sensing and actuation. This presentation will summarize recent achievements by this team and how they support the technology and concept maturation of HWO.

Items.Authors: Deniz Ölçek, Tore André Bekkeng, John Rune Jakobsen, Fredrik Harring Mathiesen, Vetle Berg Abrahamsen, Halvor Strøm, Georg Magneshaugen, Ha Hoang, Mustafa Najjar, Jennifer Travanca, Vidar Espeland, Simen Harnes, Mattias Carlqvist, Pekka Tapio Neuvonen
Items.Title: Advancing modular space avionics: design and development of an ADHA payload controller module for PICU
Items.Abstract: The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) is an ESA initiative to establish a compact and modular avionics framework for future space missions. Within this architecture, the Payload Interface Controller Unit (PICU) provides centralized instrument control, data handling, and timing distribution. This work presents the design and development efforts of the Payload Controller Module (PCM), a key building block of the PICU responsible for sensor interfacing and payload command management. We outline the PCM’s role within the PICU, the motivation behind its modular design, and the progress toward its engineering model. The work demonstrates how ADHA’s reusable avionics approach can streamline payload development and support a broad range of scientific and Earth-observation missions.

Items.Authors: Shannon M. Duff, Jason E. Austermann, Kyuyoung Bae, Johannes Hubmayr, Gregory Jaehnig, Michael J. Link, Tammy J. Lucas, Christopher Rooney, Corwin Shiu, Joel Ullom
Items.Title: Advancing TES bolometer performance for next-generation CMB instruments
Items.Abstract: The feedhorn-coupled planar-orthomode-transducer (OMT)-fed transition-edge sensor (TES) bolometer has been demonstrated in large-format arrays for multiple successful Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarimetry experiments spanning frequencies from 20-300 GHz. We report on a set of test pixel measurements aimed to advance the detector performance for the next generation CMB instrument through better understanding of the efficiency of each mm-wave component in the circuit. Additional development of a calibration TES based on the superconducting proximity effect to set its properties will lead to increased dynamic range for in-lab optical loading. We will present details of the design, fabrication, and characterization of these test pixels.

Items.Authors: Sofia Fatigoni
Items.Title: Aliased noise characterization in BICEP array 150GHz and 220/270GHz time-division multiplexed detectors
Items.Abstract: We analyze the performance of the BICEP Array 150 GHz TES detectors with a focus on noise behavior. Early observations showed excess noise from the TDM readout, where high-frequency fluctuations are aliased into the 0.1–1 Hz science band. We trace this excess to elevated TES loop gain, driven by a steep α, which speeds detector response but amplifies out-of-band noise that is then aliased. Using 400 kHz open-loop noise spectra, we identify this high-frequency excess and compute its expected aliased contribution. We show that reducing loop gain, by operating the focal plane at slightly higher temperature or by increasing the multiplexing rate, effectively mitigates the noise. NET tests confirm that running ~100 mK above nominal improves stability and reduces NET by ~10%. These results highlight the link between TES parameters, noise performance, and overall sensitivity for next-generation CMB polarimeters.

Items.Authors: Gizay Yolalan, Derya Öztürk Çetni, Bülent Güçsav, Ebru Uzunçam, Onur Şatır, Elif Köksal, Cahit Yeşilyaprak, Joackim Defigueiredo, Laurent Jolissaint
Items.Title: Alignment and performance evaluation of the K-mirror field stabilization system of the DAG400 telescope
Items.Abstract: The DAG400 Telescope, designed with an alt-azimuth configuration, requires correction of optical field rotation  during astronomical tracking. To address this, a K-mirror field stabilizer (KORAY) was developed and integrated  between the tertiary mirror (M3) and scientific instruments. This paper presents the alignment methodology,  iterative adjustment algorithm, and preliminary performance results of the KORAY system. Using both laser  based internal alignment and starlight-based external alignment, the system achieved a reduction of orbital  diameter from 680 pixels to 400 pixels ( 2 mm), demonstrating sufficient accuracy for short-exposure observations.  Future improvements will focus on long-exposure stability through integration with telescope tracking and control  systems.

Items.Authors: Joshua D. Fitzpatrick, Christopher B. Mendillo
Items.Title: Analysis of atmospheric wavefront distortions from PICTURE, a balloon-based optical telescope
Items.Abstract: PICTURE-D is a NASA balloon mission intended to directly image debris disks in nearby star systems. The observatory floats at altitudes up to 40km, above 99% of Earth’s atmosphere. This greatly reduces the effects of atmospheric turbulence and seeing, allowing for much more stable stellar wavefronts. To counteract turbulence, most modern optical telescopes utilize various adaptive optics (AO) systems. Many AO systems observe the incoming signal with wavefront sensors and aim to correct the effects of atmospheric distortion in near real-time with deformable mirrors. Although greatly reduced by altitude, PICTURE-D must still contend with these distortions as well as effects from thermal and mechanical deformations and imperfections in optical components. During three flights in 2019, 2022 and 2025, the mission has collected a vast amount of wavefront sensor data, detailing exactly what errors were present and at what times. We present an analysis of the wavefront distortions and attempt to connect them to various sources both interior to the instrument and exterior from the atmosphere. Emphasis is placed on atmospheric turbulence and the simulation of atmospheric distortions at high altitudes. The feasibility of AO corrections is also discussed, centering on the size of distortions and the timescale over which they vary.

Items.Authors: Christoph Baranec, Reed Riddle, Yuhei Takagi, James Lyke
Items.Title: Analysis of laser-satellite deconfliction for astronomical observatories
Items.Abstract: We present an analysis of laser-satellite deconfliction across three astronomical laser observatories for right ascension and declination targets and fixed azimuth and elevation ranges. This study uses new visualization tools to evaluate how different science exposure durations impact the total percentage of available open-time during observing nights. We further assess the operational efficiency of laser keep-out-cone half-angles from the default 2.5 degrees down to the 0.1-degree minimum. We also directly compare the open-time differences of right ascension and declination targets vs. fixed azimuth and elevation ranges. Finally, we analyze historical trends to quantify the growing effect of satellite mega-constellations and the efficacy of specific waiver protocols on ground-based laser astronomy.

Items.Authors: F. Tenegi, O. Tubío Araújo, R. Simoes
Items.Title: Analytical, FEMs, and experimental study of natural frequencies of subsystems of the laser guide star for GTC
Items.Abstract: The LGS Facility (LGSF) for GTC generates an artificial star (Laser Guide Star or LGS) in the high atmosphere to help the GTCAO system correct for atmospheric turbulence. The LGSF's core is a high-power laser operating at the Na D2 line (589 nm). This beam is expanded and routed by the Laser Transfer System (LTS) to the Laser Launch Telescope (LLT), which points and launches it into the sky. The light stimulates sodium (Na) atoms in the mesosphere, causing them to emit photons and thus creating the LGS.  The aim of this talk is to present both analytical and finite element studies, as well as experimental results regarding the eigenfrequencies of some of the main subsystems of the GTCAO LGS system.

Items.Authors: M. Landoni, M. A. Monteiro, P. Di Marcantonio, A. Zanutta, L. Origlia, E. Mason, R. Cirami, V. Baldini, A. Balestra, G. Calderone, I. Coretti, G. Cupani, A. Feltre, V. C. Geers, A. A. Järvinen, A. Kaminski, J. Knoche, J. Liske, M. MacIntosh, M. Malve, T. Marquart, A. Marconi, M. Porru, N. Sanna, A. Scaudo, D. Sosnowska
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: the software ecosystem
Items.Abstract: In this paper, we present an overview of the software architecture designed for the ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph (ANDES), developed in preparation for the instrument Preliminary Design Review (PDR). We provide a quick overview of the control software, as it is already presented in detail in another paper of this Conference, outlining how it has been conceived to ensure reliable operation of a complex, highly distributed instrument such as ANDES. Then, we describe the suite of science-oriented software tools that will accompany ANDES and support its use by scientists. These include the Exposure Time Calculator, the Observation Preparation tools, and the Data Reduction Library functionalities that are crucial for efficient planning and for the systematic processing of raw data produced by the instrument.

Items.Authors: Fabio Rossi, Enrico Pinna, Guido Agapito, Giulia Carlà, Nicolò Azzaroli, Ben Buky, Cédric Taïssir Héritier
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: updates from the prototyping work package of the SCAO module
Items.Abstract: The ANDES SCAO module for the ELT spectrograph is undergoing prototyping to validate key components and algorithms. Simulation work assessed two piston-sensing concepts for the reference path: a double-wavelength LIFT sensor (modeled in SPECULA) and a photonic-lantern–based approach (analyzed using a GPU-optimized waveguides simulator). In parallel, the SPRINT algorithm, designed to track Pyramidal Wavefront Sensor (PyWFS) misregistration, was developed and successfully validated on-sky at the Large Binocular Telescope. The experimental results demonstrated SPRINT's robustness for real-time control, guiding its integration into the SCAO architecture. These activities collectively advance the technical readiness and inform crucial design decisions for the ANDES SCAO module.

Items.Authors: Menghao Wang, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Anti-collision detection system based on precise feedback control in LAMOST
Items.Abstract: LAMOST(Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopy Telescope) is an Extremely Large Active Reflective Schmidt Telescope located in Hebei, China. In the past few years we are working on a new generation LAMOST fiber position system. The new system has more fibers, totally different communication system, and a newly designed feedback control system. With this new system, we are able to solve a problem haunting us for years, that is the collision between fiber control units. Collision can cause severe damage to fiber control units, but there was little we can do to solve it. In the new system, we designed a precise real-time close-loop feedback control system. With this system, not only can we detect fibers' real-time position, but we can also make rapid precise responses. This paper mainly introduces the precise feedback control system, and the anti-collision strategies.

Items.Authors: Adrián Calzadilla González, Nicolás Adrián Rodríguez-Linares, Luz Maria Montoya Martínez, Noelia Feijóo Amoedo, Yolanda Martín Hernando
Items.Title: AOStudio: A Software Framework for Configuration and Real-Time Visualization of Solar Adaptive Optics Simulations
Items.Abstract: A new graphical user interface (GUI) is presented for the Solar Adaptive Optics Simulator SAOS. Current AO simulation pipelines typically require direct coding, limiting accessibility and slowing prototyping. The GUI allows users to configure complete adaptive optics systems without programming, using drag-and-drop components for atmospheric modules, deformable mirrors, Shack-Hartmann sensors, and scientific cameras. It also provides interactive visualization of wavefront maps, surface deformation profiles, and performance metrics. The system follows a modular MVVM architecture, improving scalability and ease of extension, and integrates seamlessly with SAOS through a data-abstraction layer. Use cases and preliminary results demonstrate usability for engineers, researchers, and students. Future work includes multi-user support, cloud execution, and machine-learning-based adaptive control.

Items.Authors: Joseph R. Eimer, Robert H. Barkhouser, Stephen A. Smee, Rolf Chini, Marek Górski, Gergely Hajdu, Albert J. Harding, Stephen C. Hope, Paulina Karczmarek, Weronika Narloch, Grzegorz Pietrzyński, Piotr Wielgórski, Josh Peebles, Ryan Dekany
Items.Title: Araucaria InfraRed Imager (AIRI) instrument design
Items.Abstract: The Araucaria InfraRed Imager (AIRI) is a new instrument designed to provide high-precision near-infrared photometry in the J, H, and Ks bands on the 2.5-m telescope at the Cerro Murphy Observatory in Chile. AIRI will enable sub-percent geometric distance measurements to eclipsing binary systems in the Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds, providing substantially improved constraints on the extragalactic distance scale and, consequently, on the Hubble constant. AIRI builds on the WHIRC camera developed for the WIYN telescope, incorporating updated cryogenic cooling, an H2RG detector array, and targeted modifications to the original optical prescription to optimize performance for the new telescope. This paper presents the AIRI instrument design, including the optical layout, opto-mechanical architecture, and control-system framework.

Items.Authors: T. L. R. Brien, M. Baghoria, C. S. Benson, P. S. Barry, M. Becerril-Tapia, S. Doyle, C. J. Dunscombe, H. Gordon-Moys, S. Rowe
Items.Title: Array-scale performance of polarisation-sensitive kinetic inductance detectors for sub-95 GHz applications
Items.Abstract: KIDs have become one of the dominant detector technologies in the far-infrared and mm-wave domains for numerous astrophysical fields. Thin-film aluminium presents a fundamental low-frequency limit to their response for KIDs made with this material of approximately 95 GHz. This limit excludes such detectors from fully exploiting 90 GHz band which is commonly studied in cosmology. We present the array-scale performance of KIDs fabricated from a composite material of aluminium and titanium to produce a transition temperature within the range 0.90-1.05 K. We present characterisation of single arrays consisting of approximately 400 KIDs fabricated on a single 100-mm silicon wafer and readout. We examine the performance of these arrays considering fundamental sensitivity, polarisation response, and on the wafer scale due to fabrication factors. We describe the packaging of the wafer and how vibrational noise is minimised. Finally, we show early results from scaling this to the 150-mm wafers

Items.Authors: Germain Garreau, Denis Defrère, Romain Laugier, Peter M. Chingaipe, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Thomas Mattheussen, Kwinten Missiaen, Johan Morren, Gert Raskin, Muhammad Salman, Wannes Verstraeten, Azzurra Bigioli, Steve Ertel, Simon Gross, Xavier Haubois, Michael Ireland, András P. Joó, Stefan Kraus, Lucas Labadie, Stephen Madden, Frantz Martinache, Alexandra Mazzoli, György Medgyesi, Ahmed Sanny, Nicolas Schuhler, Jeremy Scott, Thomas Stuber, Bart Vandenbussche
Items.Title: Asgard/NOTT: cryogenic characterization of the mid-infrared photonic chip
Items.Abstract: Asgard/NOTT is the first long-baseline nulling interferometer that will be operational in the southern hemisphere. It is an L’-band (3.5-4µm) instrument optimized to characterize hot exozodiacal dust and young giant planets orbiting around the snowline of nearby main-sequence stars. NOTT uses a photonic beam combiner made of Gallium Lanthanum Sulfide (GLS), manufactured at Macquarie University and characterized at ambient temperatures at Universität zu Köln. Using the test bench of the NOTT instrument assembled at KU Leuven, and its test cryostat, we successfully cooled the chip down to ~140K and performed its first cryogenic characterization. The results show that the GLS photonic chip behaves as expected at cryogenic temperatures. We investigate an anti-reflection coating to reduce its Fresnel losses and increase its throughput to ~50%, and we test the coating’s resistance at cryogenic temperature

Items.Authors: John C. Wilson, Randolph P. Hammond, Robert Barkhouser, Stephen A. Smee, Nancy J. Chanover, Miranda van Iersel, Brooklyn K. McLaughlin, Noah S. Measells
Items.Title: ASPEN fore-optics preliminary design
Items.Abstract: We present the preliminary design of the fore-optics for the ARC SPectrograph for Echelle iNvestigations (ASPEN), a new optical echelle slit spectrograph for the Astrophysical Research Consortium (ARC) 3.5-m Telescope at Apache Point Observatory in New Mexico.  ASPEN will feature high throughput, particularly in the blue, with simultaneous wavelength coverage of 340 -- 1000 nm wavelength range.  Based on slit choice, the spectrograph will have user-selectable resolutions from 32,000 to 64,000.  Located after an Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (ADC), the fore-optics include a retractable calibration feed module, tip-tilt stabilization module, and retractable iodine cell. The tip-tilt system is integral to our goal of maximizing overall instrument throughput. We review the optical and opto-mechanical designs of each module.  We also discuss the slit viewer and prototypes of a two-slice image slicer module that will be located in the slit mechanism.

Items.Authors: Fulvio Gianotti, Ismam Abu, Marcello Lodi, Alessandro Tacchini, Giuseppe Malaspina, Marco De Benedetto, Federico Fiordoliva, Marco Costi, Giordano Mancini, Daniele Gregori, Mirco Pinetti, Massimo Sardo, Matteo Rosi, Davide Obbi, Pietro Bruno, Andrea Bulgarelli, Luca Castaldini, Vito Conforti, Mattia Corpora, Alessandro Costa, Valentina Fioretti, Valentina Giordano, Andrea Giuliani, Stefano Gallozzi, Christine Grivel, Simone Iovenitti, Federico Incardona, Nicola La Palombara, Giuseppe Leto, Fabrizio Lucarelli, Andrea Mandica, Emilio Mastriani, Kevin Munari, Tara Nadal, Giovanni Pareschi, Nicolò Parmiggiani, Valerio Pastore, Federico Russo, Pierluca Sangiorgi, Salvatore Scuderi, Sebastiano Spinello, Gino Tosti
Items.Title: ASTRI Mini-Array on-site ict infrastructure for high-availability and efficient SCADA operations
Items.Abstract: The ASTRI Mini-Array is an array of nine dual-mirror Cherenkov telescopes installed at the Teide Observatory, where seven telescopes are already deployed and two are acquiring Cherenkov data. Its operations rely on a dedicated on-site ICT infrastructure designed to support control, data acquisition, monitoring, and timing distribution. The system integrates a virtualized environment for telescope control, high-throughput bare-metal acquisition coupled with BeeGFS storage, Kubernetes-based services for monitoring and data quality assessment, and a White Rabbit timing network ensuring nanosecond synchronization. The infrastructure is now fully operational and has been extensively used by the AIV/T and SCADA teams during commissioning, providing critical feedback for optimization and validating its reliability for long-term scientific operations.

Items.Authors: Boon-Kok Tan
Items.Title: Band-splitting diplexing-hybrid for dual-band simultaneous-observing sideband-separating heterodyne mixers
Items.Abstract: Superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) receivers are vital for black-hole imaging with the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), which uses a global mm/sub-mm array to form an Earth-sized interferometer. Future EHT expansions demand simultaneous multi-band capability to capture rapid variability near the event horizon, support multi-line spectroscopy, and enable phase-transfer calibration from lower to higher frequencies. Although space missions use free-space diplexers for multi-band operation, their loss at ambient temperature makes them unsuitable for high-sensitivity ground-based systems. A prior cryogenic design by Masui et al. (PASJ 2021) showed that multi-band partitioning is feasible using three cascaded waveguide diplexers. Building on this, we introduce a new architecture that provides simultaneous dual-band, continuously tunable RF coverage with sideband separating operation in both bands, requiring only one set of quadrature hybrids and filters.

Items.Authors: Erik Sundin, Leif Helldner, Magnus Strandberg, Igor Lapkin, Rolf Ahlman, Mathias Fredrixon, Sven-Erik Ferm, Denis Meledin, François Joint, Alexey Pavolotsky, Victor Belitsky, Vincent Desmaris
Items.Title: Beam characterization system for cartridge‑type cryogenic THz receivers
Items.Abstract: The Group for Advanced Receiver Development (GARD) designs components and receiver front ends for millimetre wave and terahertz radio astronomy observatories. To ensure optimal performance, both components and receiver systems must be characterized under cryogenic conditions using various measurement techniques. A critical aspect of this process is the investigation of receiver optics, which ensures precise alignment and maximum sensitivity. We present a refurbished and redesigned beam measurement system, upgraded with improved hardware to enhance accuracy and reliability. The system supports measurements in the 275–373 GHz range and is adaptable to other frequency bands. To automate routines, a dedicated graphical user interface (GUI) has been developed, built upon the GARD Measurement System (GMS), a hardware abstraction layer enabling communication with instruments and data acquisition. At the conference, we will present the updated design, the GUI software, and obtained results.

Items.Authors: C. Coote, J. Zheng, Z. Cai, J. Moller, H. McGregor, J. Lawrence, S. Smedley, N. Cerneaz, R. Giroud, F. Laurent, A. Jeanneau, J. Richard
Items.Title: BlueMUSE splitting and relay optics: design strategies for a sixteen-channel blue-optimised IFU spectrograph
Items.Abstract: BlueMUSE is a blue-optimised, medium spectral resolution, panoramic integral field spectrograph under development for the Very Large Telescope (VLT). The project is now entering design phase. With an optimised transmission down to 350nm, spectral resolution of R~3500 on average across the wavelength range, and a large FoV (1 arcmin2), BlueMUSE will open up a new range of galactic and extragalactic science cases facilitated by its specific capabilities.    Centrally in the beam path, the splitting and relay optics divide the field into sixteen channels and form intermediate images for the integral field units. This contribution presents the preliminary optical design, strategy and mechanical layout, using air-spaced crystalline-glass achromat pairs to deliver the required optical performance, stability and channel clearance.

Items.Authors: Daniel Bodenmüller, Kalaga Madhav, Martin M. Roth, Philipp Huke
Items.Title: BluePOCO: a tunable visible frequency comb from microring resonators for astronomical spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Frequency combs have emerged as powerful tools for high-precision wavelength calibration in astronomical spec-  troscopy, enabling unprecedented accuracy and long-term stability. Here, we propose and numerically investigate an optical signal processing chain for generating a tunable frequency comb in the visible spectral range for the characterization and calibration of astronomical spectrographs with a Doppler accuracy of 1 m s−1 . The optical signal chain starts with a near-infrared frequency comb in the H-band, which is then down-converted into a second frequency comb centered at 780.7 nm and a third comb centered at 520.47 nm using two barium borate crystals. For this down-conversion process, a numerical model was developed that predicts a minimum spectral coverage of 32.7 nm for the second comb and 25.3 nm for the third comb. The calculated photon flux at the boundaries of the covered wavelength range of the third comb is 6.2 × 10 photons per second.

Items.Authors: Dirk Schmidt
Items.Title: Blur: a fast simulation for AO modeling and control systems testing
Items.Abstract: Blur is an adaptive optics (AO) software presenting third-party AO (realtime) control software (RTC) with simulated images of multiple wide-field Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensors (WFS).    It simulates turbulence and multiple deformable mirrors (DMs) including anisoplanatism in the subaperture images caused by turbulence and DMs far away from the pupil. Arbitrary extended or point objects can be used in the WFSs. Blur can also simulate the AO corrected “science image” of the scenery and compute wavefront errors within.    Blur is useful for AO performance modeling as well as for testing of AO RTC systems. It offers CoaXPress, CameraLink, Shared Memory and TCP interfaces for exchanging image and actuator data with the RTC. The RTC may run on the same or on a separate computer.     Blur is fast. It only takes 30 ms to simulate one update in the entire Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope multi-conjugate AO system (9 WFSs, 11817 subapertures, 3 DMs) on a 256-core AMD Epyc Zen 5 server.

Items.Authors: Kenta Yoneta, Jun Nishikawa, Yutaka Hayano, Masatsugu Iribe, Naoshi Murakami
Items.Title: Both-side dark hole generation technique based on Speckle Area Nulling (SAN)
Items.Abstract: Wavefront sensing and control (WFSC) is one of the key techniques for high-contrast imaging of exoplanets, suppressing scattered stellar light caused by wavefront aberrations to generate a dark hole. Speckle Area Nulling (SAN) method is the WFSC technique that does not require an optical propagation model in the high contrast imaging system. We have been developing the enhanced SAN method that can generate dark holes on both sides in the focal plane using two wavefront control devices, such as deformable mirrors. As a result of numerical simulations, the proposed method successfully generated both-side dark holes and achieved the stellar suppression performance equivalent to that of one-side dark hole generated by the conventional SAN method.

Items.Authors: Yulei Ding, Zhongdong Yin, Changxi Yang, Chengying Bao
Items.Title: Bright Dirac soliton microcomb in aluminum nitride microresonator
Items.Abstract: We demonstrate bright Dirac soliton microcombs in high‑Q AlN microresonators. Broadband anomalous dispersion is created via spatial mode interactions between TE00 and TM10 modes. Stable solitons are generated with an on‑chip pump power of 150 mW in a microresonator featuring a low FSR of 113 GHz for AlN microcombs. Polarization‑resolved spectroscopy experimentally verifies the mode composition of the Dirac soliton for the first time, in excellent agreement with theory. This work enables bright soliton generation in normally dispersive crystalline platforms and advances AlN‑based integrated nonlinear photonics.

Items.Authors: Félix Gudin, Nicolas Forget
Items.Title: Broadband heterodyne detection with ultrafast laser for stellar interferometry
Items.Abstract: Heterodyne interferometry enables coherent signal combination from distant telescopes, but its use at optical wavelengths is limited by photodetector electronic bandwidth. Using a mode-locked femtosecond laser to generate a train of highly chirped pulses as the Local Oscillator (LO), instead of a single-frequency laser, allows wideband detection over ~1 THz of optical bandwidth with a single detection channel. The method scales easily to multichannel detection with the same LO. We demonstrate this using a two-arm, fiber-based heterodyne interferometer in the H-band (1.56 µm) with a single detection channel. The system uses telecom-grade components, 22 GHz photodetectors, and a digital oscilloscope. Fringe visibility is retrieved through direct numerical correlation without electronic delay lines. The achieved SNR allows observing the brightest H-band stars with ~1 m² collecting area telescopes and short integration time (<100 ms).

Items.Authors: Pietro Ferraiuolo, Runa Antonio Briguglio Pellegrino, Guido Agapito, Jean-Pierre Véran
Items.Title: Building a catalog of visually-close binary stars through Gaia PSF simulations for ELT era AO systems
Items.Abstract: Close binary stars with separations of 20–200 mas can distort NGS asterisms, introduce centroiding bias, and reduce the stability and performance of adaptive optics systems. The BINCAT project aims to build a dedicated catalog of such binaries to support AO operations, serving both as a blacklist for NGS selection and as a benchmark set for testing next-generation systems. Because resolving binaries at these separations requires ≥8 m telescopes with AO, we identify candidates by exploiting Gaia DR3 binarity indicators and by developing a simulator capable of reproducing Gaia’s detection flags. The simulator provides the probability of binarity and estimates key parameters such as separation and magnitude contrast. Candidate binaries can then be validated through commissioning data from instruments at the ELT (MORFEO/MICADO, ANDES), other AO-equipped facilities, and archival observations, enabling iterative refinement of the catalog.

Items.Authors: Davide Mollica, Osvaldo Catalano, Giovanni Contino, Milvia Capalbi, Mattia Corpora, Fabio Paolo Lo Gerfo, Pierluca Sangiorgi, Giuseppe Sottile, Francesco Casini, Stefano Germani, Giuseppe Leto, Giancarlo Cusumano, Teresa Mineo, Gino Tosti, Salvatore Scuderi, Giovanni Pareschi
Items.Title: Calibration of the ASTRI-1 and ASTRI-3 Cherenkov cameras
Items.Abstract: The ASTRI Mini-Array is an international project, led by the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), that aims to deploy an array of nine 4 m-diameter Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes. It is designed to study astronomical sources emitting in the very high-energy range, from 1 TeV to 200 TeV. We have installed seven telescopes out of nine, and two of them already acquire Cherenkov data, undergoing the commissioning and science verification phase. Each telescope is equipped with a Cherenkov camera based on Silicon Photomultipliers, which features an embedded calibration system that consists of two laser diodes coupled to a side-emitting optical fiber. This system enables on-site extraction of calibration coefficients for data analysis and camera configuration. In this contribution, we describe the camera calibration performed during the commissioning phase of the two operational telescopes and the system stability monitoring conducted through daily calibration run.

Items.Authors: Breann N. Sitarski, Jessie L. Dotson, Jonathan C. Papa, Paul A. Scowen, Scott Gaudi, Milan Mandić, Alan B. Gostin, Michael W. McElwain, Rob Zellem, Jessica Noviello, Aki Roberge, Alden S. Jurling, Richard J. Cartwright
Items.Title: Capabilities for the Habitable Worlds Observatory’s high-resolution imager
Items.Abstract: The HWO Technology Maturation Project Office (HTMPO) recently released a call for US-led studies for instruments for transformative astrophysics, including a NUV/Optical/NIR high spatial resolution imager (HRI). HRI could have many potential modes, including astrometry, imaging, and low-resolution spectroscopy, while also fulfilling the guiding and some wavefront sensing modes for the entire observatory. The proposed HRI concepts are meant to be responsive to a wide range of astrophysics science cases detailed by the community. The call for instrument studies defines bounding conditions for mass, power, and volume, as well as information about the optical, thermal, and mechanical interfaces for EACs 4 and 5.  The HRI Coordination Group developed these bounding conditions while incorporating science and engineering feedback, which we include in this presentation. NASA supports collaborative efforts for instrument studies, both internal to the US and abroad.

Items.Authors: Paul Tagnon, Damien Prele, Manuel Gonzalez, Michel Piat, Alessandro Monfardini, Martino Calvo, Emile Prele, Faouzi Boussaha
Items.Title: Capacitively coupled lambda/4 shorted resonator filters in a fully coplanar superconducting CPW spectrometer
Items.Abstract: In this work, we present the design of a fully coplanar waveguide back shorted dual quarter wavelength spectrometer.  The dual quarterwave length is equivalent to a long open transmission line where we added a shunt inductance to create a high frequency quarter wavelength on one side (filter) and a readout frequency quarter wavelength on the other side (MKID).  Adding a backshort to the feedline increases the transmitted power up to near 100% to the MKID.  We first present a simple circuit equivalent of the proposed spectrometer and the optimizations methods used.  Then the model was implemented on Sonnet where we considered the main fabrication constraints.

Items.Authors: Rémi Soummer, Iva Laginja, Emiel Por, Raphaël Pourcelot, Sarah Steiger, Bryony Nickson, Alexis Lau, Pierre Baudoz, Jules Fowler, Raphaël Galicher, Tyler Groff, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Dimitri Mawet, Johan Mazoyer, Michael McElwain, Lane Meier, Axel Potier, Laurent Pueyo, Susan Redmond, Scott Will, Neil Zimmerman
Items.Title: CATKit2-HCI: a collaborative framework for advancing high-contrast coronagraph testbeds
Items.Abstract: High-contrast exoplanet imaging requires dedicated laboratory testbeds for coronagraph technology development. The CATKit2-High-Contrast-Imaging (CATKit2-HCI) international collaboration unites groups operating coronagraph testbeds using CATKit2, an open-source Python infrastructure controlling hardware via a fast, C++ Client-Server architecture.   Our goal is to develop and share a common architecture and tools across facilities, fostering collaboration and accelerating progress. A key objective is to avoid duplication of effort and facilitate more direct comparison of results obtained at different testbeds. We are developing a common framework for wavefront sensing and control, standardized file outputs, visualization, and performance metrics. Formalized by a Collaboration Agreement, this initiative also facilitates the exchange of students and postdoctoral researchers, and is open to expand to other high-contrast coronagraph testbeds.

Items.Authors: Abigail White, Daniel Fabricant, Charlie Conroy, Joseph Zajac, Vedant Candra
Items.Title: Characterization of connectors for the Viaspec optical fibers
Items.Abstract: The Via Project will constrain the nature of dark matter by measuring velocity perturbations within cold stellar streams, characterize the faintest dwarf galaxies, and tense cold gas structure in the Milky Way halo. Achieving these science goals requires high resolution spectroscopy with a radial velocity accuracy of ~100 m/s. To accomplish this, Via will deploy twin fiber positioning systems and multi-object, fiber-fed spectrographs on the 6.5-meter MMT and Magellan/Clay telescopes. We present the design of the Viaspec fiber system and evaluate the focal ratio degradation and throughput performance of a commercial fiber connector. We measure a 4.4% median connector throughput loss, demonstrating that tightly toleranced commercial connectors are promising for astronomical use.

Items.Authors: Paul Hickson, Micah Piva, Shaojie Chen, Suresh Sivanandam
Items.Title: Characterization of Kr and Xe pencil-type spectral lamps for the GIRMOS calibration system
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Infrared Multi-Object Spectrograph (GIRMOS) is an integral-field spectrometer for the Gemini North observatory. Working with the Gemini North Adaptive Optics system, it will have a multi-object adaptive optics capability to provide increased resolution and sensitivity. The GIRMOS Calibration System (CAL) integrated within the GIRMOS instrument, provides photometric, spectroscopic and metrology calibration. For spectroscopic calibration, CAL will employ long-life (5,000 hr) Kr and Xe pencil-type gas discharge lamps. In order to characterize the emission from these lamps, we have performed laboratory measurements covering the wavelength range 900 - 2500 nm. Here we report absolute fluxes for the 145 most-prominent spectral lines in this region, spanning three orders of magnitude in intensity. The results confirm the suitability of these lamps for GIRMOS.

Items.Authors: Christian Fruck, Felipe Pedreros Bustos, Petr Janout, David Alaluf, Ronald Holzlöhner, Pierre Haguenauer, David R. Jenkins, Julienne Böttger, Mauro Centrone, Marco Faccini
Items.Title: Characterization of Rayleigh backscattering in CaNaPy: a sodium-LGS pulsed monostatic system
Items.Abstract: CaNaPy is an experimental Laser Guide Star (LGS) Adaptive Optics facility at the 1m ESA OGS telescope at the Observatorio del Teide, developed at ESO in collaboration with ESA, Durham University, IAC, INAF, and Microgate, with scientific collaborators from ANU and the RICAM institute. It aims for demonstrating pre-compensation of a sodium LGS uplink beam using a Pyramid wavefront sensor in a monostatic system.  In a monostatic system, one of the main challenges is to prevent laser stray light from the uplink path and Rayleigh scattering from reaching the wavefront sensor. This goal requires precisely synchronized mechanical chopper wheels in the up- and downlink optical paths. To gain detailed knowledge of the temporal properties of the return signal and to further fine tune the design and timing of the chopper wheels, the received pulses are sampled with a photomultiplier tube. We highlight technical aspects of the implementation and report on first measurements using this approach.

Items.Authors: Vianak Naranjo, Thomas Bertram, Yared Reinarz, Maximilian Haeberle, Arne Bramigk, Harry Marth, Wim Pessemier
Items.Title: Characterization of the cryogenic METIS SCAO modulator
Items.Abstract: The METIS SCAO modulator is a motorized cryogenic tip-tilt mirror in charge of high precision circular motion that has to be synchronized with the integration time of the wavefront sensor detector, reaching up to 1000 circles per second. We present the results of the ongoing characterization of the modulator under cryogenic conditions, showing that the prototype not yet complies with the specification of the SCAO module at the required operating temperature of 70K.

Items.Authors: Huatao Zhang, Youwei Xie, Dejing Ni, Liang Wang, Fujia Du, Kai Zhang, Jean Louis Lizon
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: design of software architecture
Items.Abstract: The Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is a next-generation visible and ultraviolet spectrograph designed for the Gran Telescopio Canarias. This paper provides an overview of the control software architecture of CHORUS, which is designed as an integral part of the GTC Control System. The main components described are the Mechanisms Control System, responsible for controlling all moving mechanisms; the Data Acquisition System, which interfaces with the detectors; the Data Factory (DF) system, tasked with data reduction, storage, and quality control; the Instrument Library, which coordinates all instrument devices for scientific observations; and the Sequencer Library, which manages the execution of complex operational and scientific sequences in close coordination with the telescope. This modular architecture will ensure a robust, scalable, and maintainable system for the lifetime of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Jing Chen, Liang Wang, Mingyi Ding, Jean Louis Lizon, Kai Zhang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: design of the exposure time calculator
Items.Abstract: The Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) will equip the Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable (CHORUS) spectrograph, offering ultraviolet and optical bands with resolving powers of R ≥ 25,000 and R ≥ 120,000, respectively. It is expected to have high-precision radial velocity measurement capabilities at the level of sub-m s−1. We developed an exposure time calculator (ETC), which is designed to assist observers, instrument scientists, and proposal planners in evaluating the expected performance of CHORUS under a wide range of observing conditions. The ETC enables efficient estimation of exposure times, achievable signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and photon-noise limited radial velocity (RV) precision. The software is implemented with Python 3, and integrates a web-based user interface to enhance usability.

Items.Authors: Liang Wang, Jing Chen, Mingyi Ding, Shengrun Liu, Jean-Louis Lizon, Kai Zhang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: end-to-end simulation of two-dimensional echelle spectrum
Items.Abstract: The Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is an echelle spectrograph to be installed on the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) in Spain. We developed an end-to-end simulation framework to generate two-dimensional spectral data for CHORUS. This framework uses spot diagrams as input and accounts for various stellar parameters. It models different observing conditions, including atmospheric transparency, seeing, airmass, and the total throughput of the instrument. The PSF at different positions on the CCD is modeled by convolving the fiber illumination profile with the optical PSF. Various noises are incorporated, including photon noise, sky background, CCD readout noise, and dark current. The simulated two-dimensional spectra are used to test the CHORUS data reduction pipeline and to refine instrument parameters. Using this framework, we concluded that the key characteristics of CHORUS can fulfill the scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Huiqi Ye, Jean Louis Lizon, Fujia Du, Zhen Tang, Kai Zhang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: fiber link and fiber scrambling
Items.Abstract: CHORUS (Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph) is a powerful science instrument under development for the 10.4m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC). It aims to detect and study habitable exoplanets by high-precision radial velocity measurement and extend the scientific research in some forefront areas such as element origin, black holes, galaxy evolution, etc., for the decade to come. To reach this scientific goal, this spectrograph provides a spectral resolution of R≥120,000 in the visible wavelength region (425–780 nm) and R≥25,000 in the near-UV range (310–425 nm) simultaneously. We present the final design of fiber link system and test results of a double-scrambler prototype and a dynamic scrambler prototype for CHORUS.

Items.Authors: Liang Tang, Jean-Louis Lizon, Qiqige Xin, Bin Yu, Jiajia Wu, Shengrun Liu, Mingda Jiang, Huiqi Ye, Kai Zhang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: final design of the calibration system
Items.Abstract: Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is a high-resolution spectroscopic instrument under development for the 10.4 m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) at La Palma, Spain. One of its main scientific drivers is the detection and characterization of extra-solar planets. The visible branch spectrograph (VIS) has a spectral resolving power of R≥120000 (425–780 nm) and is vacuum stabilized for performing high precision radial velocity (RV) measurements. The UV branch spectrograph (UVS) has a spectral resolving power of R≥25000 (310–425 nm) and allows for stellar activity monitoring. Aiming at a radial velocity precision at the sub-m/s level, CHORUS has a dedicated calibration system enabling high precision calibration under different observation modes. This paper reports on the final design and prototyping work of the CHORUS calibration system (CLS).

Items.Authors: Kai Zhang, Shengrun Liu, Yuan Liang, Liang Wang, Qiqige Xin, Jean-Louis Lizon, Yongtian Zhu
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: optical design of the UV band spectroscopic chain
Items.Abstract: The Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is a high-precision spectrograph developedfor the 10.4 m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC). The instrument employs a dual-band configuration, combining an ultraviolet spectrograph (UVS) with a visible-band spectrograph (VIS), to optimize performance for faint-object detection in the UV and for extreme precision radial velocity (EPRV) measurements in the visible band. This paper presents a complete optical chain of UVS, from the Nasmyth focus to the science detectors, in which the UVS is fed by fore-optics rather than a fiber link. This design delivers a spectral resolution of R ≥ 25,000 over the wavelength range 310–425 nm, offering competitive performance for ultraviolet spectroscopic observations. The capability will support studies of stellar activity relevant to EPRV science and will also enable frontier research in areas such as Galactic archaeology.

Items.Authors: Kai Zhang, Bernard Delabre, Jean-Louis Lizon, Liang Wang, Shengrun Liu, Yuan Liang, Qiqige Xin, Xuesong Wang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: optical design of the visible band spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The CHORUS is a high-precision spectrographic facility for the 10.4m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) at La Palma, Canarias, Spain. The VIsible band Spectrograph (VIS), which is the most important subsystem in the CHORUS, will provide the powerful competitiveness of Extreme Precision Radial Velocity (EPRV) measurement for searching habitable exoplanets, studying planetary atmosphere, and others. Its optics are composed of a pupil slicer unit and an anamorphic white-pupil system with two spectral arms (Green and Red). The VIS enables providing high-resolution of R≥120,000 over the wavelength range from 425nm to 780nm. The paper documents the way to provide the required spectral resolution by using the anamorphic pupil slicer and a mosaic echelle grating, and also accommodate all the spectra from 2 parallel science fibers by two large 9K detectors. Its optical performance and instrument specifications are verified by the corresponding simulations and analysis.

Items.Authors: Fujia Du, Shuai Chen, Hao Chen, Huatao Zhang, Dejing Ni, Jiajia Wu, Kai Zhang, Jean-Louis Lizon
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: the final design of instrument control electronics
Items.Abstract: CHORUS (Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph) is a high-resolution, ultra-stable spectrograph to be installed on the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC). Its key feature is achieving an instrumental radial velocity precision of sub m s-1. This is an extremely demanding performance target that drives the design of its subsystems. The CHORUS Instrument Control Electronics (ICE) is responsible for governing all instrument subsystems, including 15 motorized stages, more than 60 sensors, and several calibration lamps. To meet CHORUS stringent requirements, this paper presents the final design of the ICE, covering its instrument and electronic architecture. It focuses on controller selection, the motion control system, and the calibration control system. It presents the test performance of core prototypes, including the image stabilization system, motion control system, and dynamic scrambler system.

Items.Authors: Dejing Ni, Huatao Zhang, Fujia Du, Huiqi Ye, Liang Wang, Liang Tang, Kai Zhang, Jean Louis Lizon
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: the image stabilization system
Items.Abstract: CHORUS (Canary Hybrid Optical High-Resolution Ultra-Stable Spectrograph) is expected to become a powerful scientific instrument for precise radial velocity measurements. This paper introduces the design of the image stabilization system of CHORUS to enhance the light acquisition ratio from the telescope. The image stabilization system utilizes image processing methods to calculate real-time centroid shifts caused by atmospheric turbulence and telescope tracking errors, then applies tip-tilt correction to maintain highly stable focusing of the scientific target's spot at the fiber-injection interface. An experimental system, comprising a seeing simulation system and an image stabilization system, was developed to validate the approach. Experimental results demonstrate the proposed system achieves a star acquisition rate of 69.9% which closely approaches 70% under the 0.8" seeing condition and 1.2" observation field.

Items.Authors: Rima Islam, Aline Dinkelaker, Abani Shankar Nayak, Kalaga V. Madhav, Martin M. Roth
Items.Title: Commissioning the AIP's ultrafast laser-inscription facility: defining the parameter space for type-I waveguide fabrication
Items.Abstract: This work details the iterative statistical optimization of the femtosecond-based ultrafast laser inscription system—specifically pulse energy, repetition rate, translation speed, and scan density to achieve Type-1 positive refractive-index modifications. We present the resulting fabrication recipe for single-mode, high-throughput waveguides optimized for the astronomical J-band (1300-1400 nm). By achieving precise Mode Field Diameter (MFD) matching with standard optical fibers, we ensure low insertion loss. The optimization of parameter space is critical for the fabrication of complex devices, such as photonic reformatters, beam combiners, and pupil remappers, for future deployment at the CHARA array and Calar Alto Observatory.

Items.Authors: M. Viveganandam, J. Adassuriya, K. P. S. C. Jayaratne
Items.Title: Compact medium-resolution spectrograph for alt-azimuth mounted Cassegrain telescopes: optical design and performance analysis
Items.Abstract: Alt-azimuth mounted telescopes with Cassegrain focus offer affordability and versatility but often lack the clearance needed to attach standard commercial spectrographs. To overcome this limitation, we developed a compact, cost-effective, medium-resolution spectrograph specifically designed for seamless integration with such telescopes. The instrument incorporates a 1200 grooves/mm diffraction grating and a narrow slit aperture, with optical performance evaluated using Zemax OpticStudio 2025 R2 ray-tracing simulations. Results confirm effective spectral dispersion, accurate focusing of RGB wavelengths, and strong agreement with theoretical expectations. Aberration analysis shows negligible higher-order effects, with only slight spherical aberration present. Overall, the spectrograph demonstrates excellent image quality and validates a practical, accessible solution for high-resolution astronomical spectroscopy.

Items.Authors: Alikhan Basheer, Devika Divakar, Pramod Panchal, Sanjeev Jha, Prasanna Deshmukh, Sudarsan Kambhala, Karthic Kumar, Sriram Sripadmanabhan
Items.Title: Comparative study of roundel support system for sub aperture metrology of segmented telescope mirrors
Items.Abstract: As a partner of the Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) project, India has agreed to supply 84 polished segments for the primary mirror, using the innovative Stressed Mirror Polishing (SMP) technology obtained from Coherent Inc., USA. Some of the metrology tools for the SMP process are designed and developed by India TMT (ITMT) team such as the 27-point whiffletree-based support system. This system acts as the support structure during the entire metrology activities of polished TMT Roundel.   The study focuses on a comparative analysis of Roundel Support systems used in one of the metrology processes, which is Sub Aperture Metrology to capture the Band 2-6 data. It contrasts results from the 43-point hydraulic-based support system at Coherent with the 27-point whiffletree-based support system developed by I-TMT. This analysis assesses efficacy and performance differences between the two support systems, involving a comprehensive examination of a 1520mm diameter polished glass roundel.

Items.Authors: Reuben Neate, Tinus Stander
Items.Title: Concept design of a single-IC integrated 183GHz direct detection water vapour radiometer
Items.Abstract: The requirements for an 183 GHz water vapour radiometer (WVR) are considered, and design specifications are proposed. The proposed design is found to be achievable through single-IC integration of a radiometer using a 165 GHz direct detection receiver, consisting of a calibration switch with controllable thermal load, low noise amplifier (LNA), and power detector. The design is found to produce a compact, lightweight WVR, suitable for integration in confined spaces. The single-IC integration also lends itself to arrayed receiver design, of which a concept is presented.
